Anya — thanks, and appreciate the clear checklist. High level response and proposed plan below.

Short answers:
- UK IDTA / UK Addendum: We can execute the standard UK Addendum to our DPA for UK-resident data; signing requires our legal review but is supported as a standard play. Alternative: we can combine SCCs + documented TIA narrative for customers who prefer that route; both options are commonly accepted by buyers.

Proposed plan & timeline:
- Today: we’ll assemble a consolidated evidence packet (one-pager + attachments) and upload to a shared Drive folder.
- Mon-Wed (May 18–20): Redwood legal to prepare DocuSign skeleton of our DPA + optional UK Addendum; technical team to prepare SCCs mapping and TIA narrative.
- Fri May 21: deliver final packet and DocuSign link.

Attachments we will provide: redwood-dpa-qa-checklist.pdf, sccs-mapping.xlsx, tia-scope-outline.pdf.

Questions for you:
- For the DocuSign skeleton, do you want the DPA with tracked redlines or a clean copy + redline summary?
- Any internal stakeholders to include on the DocuSign routing (legal + procurement usually suffices)?

I’ve copied Kim and Rishi to align on the evidence items and technical notes. I’ll own the external delivery and DocuSign cadence.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345) and I’ll place the packet in the Drive link I’ve added to related_links.

Subject: Re: Initial evidence ask and DPA question (technical evidence & ops notes)

On Sat, May 16, 2026 at 09:12 AM Anya Petrova <anya@healthsync.io> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo earlier — HealthSync is moving quickly on the procurement side and we need to close the data transfer and DPA items before legal signs off.

Quick ops / evidence notes for the packet — picked items that procurement typically asks for so we don't over-send:

Essential deliverables (one consolidated zip + one-page summary):
- SOC 2 Type II coverage statement (current year) — we provide the AICPA letter + scope note.
- Subprocessor registry CSV with roles and locations (we redact internal contact emails).
- SCCs mapping spreadsheet (sccs-mapping.xlsx) showing which clause maps to our controls and subprocessors.
- TIA narrative (tia-scope-outline.pdf) — short (1–2 pages) describing technical measures, onshore fallback, and routing safeguards.
- Network diagram (high level) and dataflow diagram (screenshots allowed).
- Retention/egress and deletion policy snippet relevant to HealthSync's data classes.

Technical caveats and asks:
- If they expect the UK Addendum signed on the redline, legal will need to review changes to our standard liability/cross-border clauses. Recommend offering a clean UK Addendum + redline summary rather than engaging in heavy redline negotiations up front.
- For the TIA, include details on pseudonymization and caching behavior (what we persist, KV cache TTLs, and how we handle deletion requests).

Logistics: I can generate the sccs-mapping.xlsx and network diagram exports by EOD Monday (May 18). Rishi — can you confirm the TIA narrative draft and whether we need any extra attestation for onshore fallback?

KG
Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference

We can do May 18 10:00 BST for a 30-minute sync to walk the packet and routing (calendar invite forthcoming). For DocuSign routing, please include Legal (anya@healthsync.io) + Procurement (procurement@healthsync.io).

- A one-line attestation about subprocessor notification cadence (how and when we notify customers of new subprocessors).

If you can hit May 21 delivery we will move to signature. Appreciate it.
